sentences.text: Meda Hanumantharao Hanumanthu, vs The State Of Andhra

Pradesh, on 4 February, 2020
Author: J. Uma Devi

Bench: J. Uma Devi
 The Hon'Ble Ms. Justice J. Uma Devi
 Criminal Petition No.597 Of 2020
Order:

-
This petition is filed under section 482 of Cr.P.C., to quash the proceedings in Crime No.207 of 2019 of Tadikonda Police Station, Guntur Urban, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328, 420 IPC and Sections 57(1), 58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short 'FSS Act, 2006) against the petitioners/A.1 to A.3, on various grounds.

2. The allegations against the petitioners briefly are that on 14.12.2019 at about 6-00 PM near Lachannagudi village of Tadikonda mandal, the complainant along with his staff on credible information seized the auto bearing No.AP 07 TE 6340 and caught hold the petitioners/A.1 to A.3,
seized the banned products under a cover of police proceedings and arrested the petitioners/A.1 to A.3.
Later, he registered the mediators report as a case in Crime No.207 of 2019 for the offences stated supra.

3. Learned counsel for petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore, the Police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the order of this Court in Crl.P.Nos.3731 of 2018 & batch, dated 27.08.2018.
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the criminal petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and SS Act.

4. So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned, as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C,
no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorise in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the F.I.R is registered suo moto filed on the report of the Sub Inspector of Police of Tadikonda Police Station.
Therefore, it is the violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IPC is concerned and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

420 IPC and Sections 57(1), 58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, Interlocutory Applications pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
